title: Location-scoped operator tokens and KMS wrapping guardrail
author: Nadia Park
release_notes: Add operator session tokens bound to region and service; enforce KMS wrapping policy for cross-region key usage; middleware injects immutable audit headers for session provenance. No user-facing API change.
description:
Motivation: Customers in regulated environments asked for stronger guarantees that operator actions (operator service accounts, platform operators, human ops) cannot be used to access keys or data outside of an explicitly pinned region. Existing RBAC v2 rules cover role bindings but do not prevent an operator token minted in one region from being used with a different CMK or from being routed through a cross-region KMS proxy. This PR implements a layered guardrail: (1) session-scoped operator tokens that encode the origin region and permitted service-bound KMS scope; (2) a KMS wrapping validator which rejects key-unwrapping requests that violate the token's declared region; (3) RBAC enforcer adjustments to treat session token attributes as first-class predicates; and (4) audit header middleware to emit immutable provenance headers for downstream indexing.

Summary of changes (high level):
- Add session token generator (api/middleware/session_scope.go) that issues short-lived JWT-like tokens with region, service, operator_id and scope claims; tokens are non-refreshable and bound to a single operator action window.
- Introduce kms/wrap/validator.go which implements server-side checks for unwrap/wrap calls; enforces a policy allowlist per-region and returns structured error codes (KMS_REGION_VIOLATION) when violated.
- Extend rbac/enforcer to consult session token claims for attribute-based decisions (rbac/enforcer.go). This allows policy like "allow operator:scale-deploy if session.region == service.region".
- Add audit/middleware/provenance_injector.go that sets X-Redwood-Provenance (signed) and X-Redwood-Region headers and marks them immutable for downstream processors.
- Add compliance doc: docs/compliance/region-token-workflow.md with example flows and threat model.
- Helm chart tweak for private installs: charts/private/values-region-pin.yaml to surface the KMS wrapping allowlist as a configurable block.

Review conversation (abridged, chronological):
- Evan Liu (Reviewer): "Overall looks solid. Two concerns: token size (we need to keep header small for streaming gateways) and whether the validator will add measurable latency for high-throughput unwrap calls. Can we micro-benchmark?"
- Nadia Park (Author): "Agree on both points. Token uses compact claims and is gzipped in transit for streaming; added benchmark harness in test/perf/kms_wrap_bench.go and attached numbers to the PR description (median +1.8ms on unwrap path under 95th percentile)."

- Priya Raman (Reviewer): "Policy semantics LGTM, but we should expose a debug metric for denied unwraps and a flag to opt-out in emergencies. Please add a metric and an operator override path with audit."
- Nadia Park (Author): "Added metrics.kms.unwrap.denied and an emergency flag kms.wrap.allow_cross_region (defaults to false for private installs). Documented emergency procedure in the compliance doc."

- Samir Patel (Reviewer): "Nit: suggest using structured audit reason codes so downstream can aggregate (e.g., reason=kms_region_violation). Also add unit tests for legacy token fallback."
- Nadia Park (Author): "Added reason codes and unit tests for legacy token path."

Performance note: micro-benchmarks (test/perf/kms_wrap_bench.go) show an additional ~1.5-3ms median latency on KMS unwrap when the validator is enabled (mostly due to claim parsing and HMAC verification). We added caching for token verification keyed by token hash with a 30s TTL which reduces impact for repeated operations.

Migration and rollout plan (ops):
1) Deploy middleware and validator in shadow mode for 48h in staging; collect metrics.kms.unwrap.denied and provenance header coverage.
2) Enable enforcement behind feature-flag for 10% of traffic in production (canary) and monitor for false positives.
3) After 72h stable canary, enable 100% and publish compliance note to accounts.

Backward compatibility: Legacy client tokens without region claims are accepted but cause the validator to fall back to a conservative deny-for-cross-region behavior (i.e., deny unwrap if target CMK region differs from request origin when no explicit consent is present). This protects customers during rollout but requires accounts to rotate to region-scoped tokens for full functionality.

Security considerations: The design minimizes risk by making tokens short-lived, non-refreshable, and tied to operator_id + action nonce. All provenance headers are signed with a server key (rotated via KMS) and cannot be overwritten by upstream. Emergency override requires a signed operator action and is auditable.

Merge outcome: PR was approved by all reviewers, CI green on green build, and merged via squash. Change log entry created and docs published to the compliance space. The private-installer chart change is gated behind a release flag and will be included in the next private release train.
